title: Cache
objective: Follow a cache miss and a cache hit, and see why cached data can go out of date.

sources.title: Microsoft Azure Architecture Center: Cache-Aside pattern

simplifies: One app, one cache, one record. Here the app does the cache work itself (the cache-aside pattern); some caches fetch from the database on their own (read-through). Real caches also expire entries after a set time and are often shared by many app servers, which makes keeping them up to date harder.

steps.caption: The app needs a user's profile. It asks the cache first, because reading from the cache is faster than asking the database.
Cache miss: the profile isn't in the cache yet, so the cache has nothing to return.

predict.prompt: This is the first time anyone has asked for this profile. What does the cache answer?

options.explanation: No. Nothing has been saved in the cache yet, so it has no copy to return.

options.text: It has nothing: a cache miss
options.explanation: Right. The cache only holds what was put in it, and this profile hasn't been yet.

options.text: It fetches the profile from the database itself
options.explanation: No. In this pattern (cache-aside) the app does the database read, not the cache.

steps.caption: So the app reads the profile from the database instead.
The app saves a copy in the cache, so the next read can skip the database.
The next time someone asks: cache hit. The answer comes straight from the cache, and the database isn't asked at all.

quiz.prompt: The profile changes in the database, but the cache still holds the old copy. What can happen?

options.text: Users may see the old profile
options.explanation: Right. That is stale data. Common fixes: remove the cached copy whenever the data changes, and give entries an expiry time.
No. The database is fine. The problem is that the cache now disagrees with it.

options.text: Nothing, the cache notices the change by itself
options.explanation: No. In this pattern the cache doesn't watch the database. The app has to remove or refresh the cached copy.

quiz.prompt: Why does the app put the profile into the cache after reading it from the database?

options.text: Because the database deletes data once it is read
options.explanation: No. Reading leaves the data in the database.

options.text: To keep a backup in case the database is lost
options.explanation: No. A cache is not a backup: its entries can expire or be removed at any time.

options.text: So the next request is a cache hit
options.explanation: Right. The next read is answered from the cache, and the database does less work.
